segments the trials from the messages and matches them to the result file by trial number. For each trial it checks the episode, the cue colour, whether an attack was shown, and the attack angle against the result file, and compares the onsets of placement, ISI and outcome (relative to the anticipation onset) and the placement duration with the times in the result file.

Of the 16,542 trials in the result files of the 92 participants with an EDF file, 16,360 are found in the EDF files, each once. The 182 missing trials are the trials after the truncation of 11872 and 5272. No EDF trial is missing from the result files.

The phase onsets agree with the result file within −7 to +2 ms (−1 to +2 ms in all but 2 trials), the placement duration within −1 to +2 ms.
The trial onsets on the EDF clock and the unix time stamps of the result file (whole seconds) differ by at most 0.57 s after a linear fit, within the resolution of the time stamps.
The task draws in degrees of visual angle around the screen centre. The slots lie on a circle of radius 8° at 0°, 11.25°, …, 348.75° (counter-clockwise from the right, as

in the result file), and the colour cue is a disc of radius 1.5° at the centre. With this convention, 82 % of the placement fixations on the circle (after drift correction) lie within half a slot of a slot that received a net in the trial; with the angles mirrored or rotated by 90°, 5–16 % do.

The pixels per degree are estimated from the placement phase: fixations whose angle lies within 5° of a slot that received a net in the trial have a median distance of 269 px from the screen centre, which gives 33.7 px per degree (89,750 fixations of the participants with gaze data who are not excluded;

The drift checks after the breaks could not always reduce the offset: some were repeated many times and accepted with large offsets (participant medians of the accepted checks 0.28–28°). The offset is therefore estimated from the data and subtracted from the gaze positions.
A block runs from one drift check or recalibration to the next (median 4 blocks per participant, 1–5).

During the placement phase the participants look at the nets they place. For every placement fixation on the circle (5–11° from the corrected centre) within half a slot (5.625°) of a slot that received a net in the trial, the difference between the raw fixation position and the slot position (8° at the slot angle) is computed. The offset of a block is the median of these differences; blocks with fewer than 30 such fixations take the participant median (9 of 322 blocks). The selection depends on the offset, so the estimate is iterated four times, starting from no offset.
The block offset is subtracted from the fixation positions (
). The offsets per block are in
, so that the same correction can be applied to the 50 Hz gaze stream. The median correction is 1.03° per participant (0.32–3.41°).

The anticipation phase is not used for the estimate. There, the colour cue is at the centre, and the median position of the fixations within 3° of the centre gives an independent offset. Before and after correction (participant medians, 90 participants with gaze data):

The distance from the placed net does not go to 0 after correction, because the fixations spread around the net (its size is 1.8° × 0.8°). Fixations within 3° of the centre take a median of 26 % of the fixation time in the anticipation phase (4–71 % across participants), and 82 % of the trials have such a fixation.
